text:
If you're wrapping up an evening out, don't put the umbrella away just yet. We're still sitting in that unsettled pattern, and while the official call keeps tonight's shower chance modest at 30%, the European and American short-range models are both running much wetter than that, closer to 90%, so a rumble of thunder or a passing shower after dark wouldn't surprise me at all. Skies stay mostly cloudy, low near 62, wind light out of the north easing off overnight.

The good news arrives with Friday. High pressure moves in and actually means it this time, so expect patchy fog to burn off into a mostly sunny day, high near 81, with just a slight lingering shower chance early on. The lake goes calm too, winds under 10 knots and waves a foot or less, so if you've been waiting for a clean paddle or sail, Friday's your window. Air quality is good. Enjoy the break, because the forecasters are already flagging widespread, potentially heavy rain moving in Sunday afternoon into Monday, with some flooding risk on saturated ground.
